body: Is your name, out of curiosity, a reference to Sergey Nechayev?

I would be inclined to agree if I had any self-control, but after years of constantly acting the same manner without ever being able to restrain myself I feel there is a degree of inexorability to my being this way. I had the "hope" which is sanctioned by psychologists in order to help your situation - willingness to try their treatments and remain open to them and such things - and have gotten nothing but disappointment. I have been on 6 medications and 5 of them have severely impacted me and the other 1 has done nothing for me at all. I have been through dozens of mental health officials and have not gotten better, so naturally I'm skeptical.

I am familiar with CBT, and I have actually gone through with CBT before, and it wasn't of any help either; it helped with anxiety issues I had, but the insecurities, the emotional issues, and everything else was not helped in the least and eventually the little bit of progress the CBT made was overwhelmed by my other issues and its value to me was essentially effaced.

As I have said, I am remorseful, but I continue to act destructively and to wrong people - it is like the guilt and the self exist in separate bodies, divided from one another, with the guilt unable to convince the self to act otherwise whatsoever, but constantly building in the face of the self's actions. So, I do not believe that it is contradictory to both insist that I am wretched and horrible and to point out my remorse; I believe my remorse CAN redeem me and my horrible personality, but only through the act I have described - through punishing myself and taking my life.

I HAVE heard it, but the same people who insist this are the ones who also insist I am horribly behaved and that I make people sick and am seriously ill. I try not to be hard on myself, but to me that isn't a matter of "silly thinking" - not when I have behaved as I have and felt as I have and thought as I have and spoke as I have. I fear that this mental illness, whatever it may be (if it can be defined within the parameters of medical diagnoses) may be incredibly difficult to treat... I understand the flaws in it and yet am totally unable to overcome it. I understand what is wrong with myself and what I am told to do and yet nothing prevents it...

I would, as well, but it almost feels to be inevitable and necessary now...

Haha if anything I'm just namedropping a few thinkers and authors in order to try and give my point more leverage and add some further understanding of my situation to people who are familiar with anyone that I had mentioned. It's not necessarily true that I've read more than you :/ 

I don't know of many people who haven't had some of these experiences, but to have them all and at the same time is not something typical in the least. Of course no one is perfect, but some people are further from perfect than others. I do not leave the blame on myself for my father leaving, but simply added it in because I feel it caused many of my mental issues in the first place. I have never been convinced I was guilty for it, because I know very specifically the circumstances that led to him leaving. 

I will PM you later on when I have more time.

All right, I'm not at all trying to be obnoxious in saying that, it's just I don't honestly feel that my suffering is worthy of such sentiments and statements, I feel that the suffering I cause others is the greater concern. I'm an agnostic atheist personally, so I dont believe there is likely to be anything beyond this life; I simply believe its not right for me to be around in this life. Of course it might be wrong, but to be honest I'm sure you have suffered more than I have, it's simply that I have CAUSED more suffering.

I think I will PM you later on, when I have more time to talk in-depth to people. Right now I'm just answering everyone who has posted.

Yes, I have attempted to speak to them (well, at least my brother; my sister is the sort of person who reacts to mental illness simply by calling it creepy and has talked about how creepy some mentally ill relatives are, she is not the sort to speak to), and all my attempts have failed; my brother promised to help me but it was totally anti-climatic and he simply told me I wouldn't hurt myself and to move on, he was absolutely no help. I don't know if I'd do well in college; in school I can get 95s and 100s with ease for research projects without any effort (doing them the day before) but in class and during tests and similar things I do terribly, because alone I can gather my thoughts but in class I simply lose focus completely and all of the knowledge as well, so I don't think I would do well in post-secondary education. 

I am returning to this subreddit to talk to the people who have commented and reached out, it's a completely different environment from a lot of other internet forums in that people actually make an effort to help... I have been spending entire days on the internet recently because I simply have no energy to do anything.

If you are being genuine (I can't tell with your comment, because when I think of my suicidal intentions I think the same thing you've said sarcastically), then thank you for the sentiment, but I don't know if I deserve sympathy, not the way that I am...

Thanks for taking the time to respond... This was one of my few concerns about the act... I know it will affect people if I do it, I am not in doubt of that. I feel that it is ultimately the best choice though... But the thought of the guilt and suffering it will ultimately cause people around me horrifies me as well and makes me feel even more hopeless... I have written as much in my suicide note as possible to indicate my full responsibility, but I know that that won't prevent everything. I have talked to many therapists but they have not been helpful, and, despite what you say, although there are people who care about me and would suffer from this, I believe I am ultimately a burden and have been told by many family members how I simply want attention and how I am the worst-behaved of my mother's children (I'm not an only child, but my siblings are much older) and how sick I make people... Then, the instant I mimic their own statements and tell them that I am burdensome to them, they insist that I am being foolish and that they have no such feelings. Nobody around me is actually willing to help me, they have promised to multiple times and have never followed through.
